utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case number IT-95-16-T, the Prosecutor of the Tribunal versus Zoran Kupreskic, Mirjan Kupreskic, Vlatko Kupreskic, Drago Josipovic, Dragan Papic, Vladimir Santic, also known as "Vlado."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Good morning. I imagine somebody is taking care of the witness. (The witness entered court)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Good morning, Captain Stevens.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Mr. Moskowitz?

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Good morning, Captain Stevens.

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Yesterday we left off with a description of your visits to Ahmici at which some burnt bodies were found in Upper Ahmici, and you ran into someone called Dragan, and saw shells around the village, and you gave your view as to what had happened in the village. I now want to turn to another visit that you made to Ahmici and ask you whether, in fact, you did make another visit to Ahmici at a later date where more bodies were found?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: I actually visited Ahmici the following day, the day after that particular day. On this occasion, we had an ambassador with us who visited the other house we were talking about yesterday. During that day, I had occasion to move around the village more freely, and then toured other buildings where I found bodies or found remains of bodies and photographed them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: And again, your estimate on the time of when this subsequent visit occurred is to the best of your recollection, with the understanding that you did have some difficulty in separating days from one another back then.

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Could you tell us what information came to the attention of BRITBAT that prompted this visit to Ahmici at the later date?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: We were getting reports from people that had survived the attack, from the people that fled. We were given reports back through the International Red Cross agencies that were already interviewing survivors and asking us to go and check particular houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Was there a particular house that came to the attention of BRITBAT that needed to be checked?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: There was a house known as House number 5. That was the address.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Did you, in fact, accompany BRITBAT to House number 5?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Could you take the pointer in front of you, and referring to the large blow-up of Ahmici behind you, just show the Court the route you took that day to House number 5?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: The route we took that day was in off the valley road, past the mosque, down into this area here, and we parked our vehicles up in this area (indicating).

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: By "this area," for the record, you're pointing to an area adjacent to the big white area in the centre of the map just a little bit towards Upper Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: That's correct. From here, House number 5 is situated past this larger structure in this area here (indicating).

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Perhaps to make the record clear on that, could you refer to Exhibit 163, which has been placed in the ELMO, or on the ELMO next to you, and if you could, with your pointer, show us where House number 5 was, and perhaps show us how you reached House number 5 from the road?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: As I mentioned, we moved through here and parked vehicles in this area (indicating). We then made our way down the side of this house here into House number 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Could you take a marker in front of you and put a circle around House number 5 for us, please?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: (Marks)

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Now, you mention there was another large structure. What was that large structure that you had referred to earlier?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: This was, I believe, slightly to the north of that, in this area here (indicating).

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Could you just put an X perhaps over that large structure, and do you recall what that large structure was?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: It was a taller, taller building, was burnt out. I couldn't describe it in more detail than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Did you, in fact, go inside House number 5?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Approximately how long did you spend inside that house on that day?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: The day I went back with the surgical team, almost all of the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Could you tell us what you saw when you entered that house, House number 5?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: When I entered the building, the building was totally gutted. The fire damage had reduced the roof right to the lowest levels. There were red tiles covering the floor, charred wooden beams; and I saw the upper body, burnt body, of an adult; and further back in the room, the other side of the room, what appeared to be the body of a smaller person, a child maybe.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Now, you mention there were red tiles on the floor of House number 5. Did you have a sense of what they were and where they came from?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: They were the tiles from the roof. In almost all of these properties, once the fire had burnt through, the roof collapsed into the lower level.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Did you see any furniture or any items inside the house other than the tiles and the remains of the bodies that you've described?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: The only furniture that was left was the furniture made out of metal, stoves, refrigerators, that type of thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: At this time, I would ask the usher to show the witness the next exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit 164.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Now, Captain Stevens, could you look at what has been marked Exhibit 164 and tell us if you recognise that?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: I recognise this as a plan of House number 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned entering a room where you saw bones and red roof tiles, or the remains of bodies and red roof tiles. Could you show us with your pointer which room you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: This room here, the largest room in the property (indicating).

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: When you say "the largest room," did you have a sense of really how large that room was?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: It was about 18 feet by 10 feet perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Do you have a recollection of where these remains were that you found when you entered House number 5?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yeah, they were at opposite ends of the big room. In this area, there was a metal stove. There was remains in this area (indicating) and near the stove.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Could you, with your marker, draw a little square to show where the stove was that you saw when you entered House number 5?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: (Marks)

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: With an X, could you show where the remains of the bodies were that you found?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: (Marks)

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Now, at this time, I would ask the usher to show the witness two exhibits that have already been entered into evidence, starting with Exhibit 86 and then followed by Exhibit 87. If you could keep the schematic, Exhibit 164, nearby the witness because we will be referring to that as we talk about these two photographs. Thank you. They don't both have to go on. They don't both have to go on the ELMO at the same time but just nearby because we will be moving back and forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Could you look at, Captain Stevens, could you look at Exhibit 86, this photograph, and tell us what that shows?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: This depicts the scene in that room. This is the metal stove and this is the main doorway into that room (indicating) and the window at the rear.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Now, you indicated that you found some human remains in a part of that house. Could you show us where you think some of those remains were, if it's depicted in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: The main one isn't, but there's a smaller area here near the stove and up in this area, maybe just off of this particular photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Now, referring back to the schematic which is Exhibit 164, just so we can get our bearings, could you show us on the schematic where you think the photographer was in Exhibit 86 when that photograph was taken, perhaps using a circle and an arrow to show where the photographer was and the point of view of that photographer?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: He would have been in this area here (indicating), looking that way (marks).

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Why do you think so?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: The stove is on the right-hand side. You can clearly see the doorway in that photograph, and you can see out the window.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Now, could you look at formerly admitted Exhibit 87, please? Could you tell us, Captain Stevens, what this picture shows?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: This picture shows the torso of a body that I mentioned earlier in the other part of the room, the same room, from the other direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Could you refer again to Exhibit 164, the schematic, and again show us where you think the photographer was in that photograph, photograph 87, with an arrow showing as well the point of view of that photographer?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: (Marks). That type of position.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Does this photograph confirm your memory or your impression that the human remains that you saw that day were, in fact, located where you placed the X?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Thank you. If you could possibly leave those three exhibits on the desk in front of the witness? We may be referring to it a little bit later.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Now, during your visit to Ahmici and your visit into House number 5, do you know whether or not a videotape was taken recording some of that visit?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: I know a video was taken, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Did you have an opportunity to view that video before coming to court today?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Could you show us on that map behind you, so that when we view the video, we will have a sense of where we are in Ahmici, where the video camera begins showing us scenes of Ahmici and where the video camera takes us until we get to House number 5?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: I'm pretty sure that the video camera shows us moving into this area. Apart from the mosque, it shows the vehicles being parked up, teams being briefed, and then people moving down towards House number 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Now, during the course of this video, do you recall whether you observed the video camera operator actually going into House number 5 and showing the inside of House number 5?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: I do recall that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: So that when we view the video, it will be clear, could you take a look again at that schematic, 164, and, if you could, show us with your pointer how you remember seeing the video camera operator entering House number 5 and what route he took inside the house?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: The video cameraman went in through the main doorway of House number 5 and took some footage of this darker area here (indicating) before moving left into the main building and observing this area and the area to the right of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: There is a shot, I believe, at the end of this videotape, showing that main room. Do you recall, and can you recall for us, where the video camera operator was as he video-cameraed or shot a video of the inside of that main room of House number 5?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: I believe he was just inside the doorway, in this general direction, facing this general direction (indicating).

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Perhaps if you could place a small dot with maybe the green marker and a small arrow to show where the video camera operator was?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: (Marks)

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Could you also show us with an arrow and a line the route of the video camera operator into House number 5, please?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: (Marks)

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: At this time, I would ask that we play the videotape.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: As we play it, if you see anything that you would like to comment on, Captain, please feel free to do so, and I will ask the film to be stopped. May we have the video? (Videotape played)

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: This shows us moving into Ahmici with the mosque on the right-hand side. The vehicles contain medical teams and a few engineers in case we uncovered mines, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Was the purpose of this visit essentially to remove the bodies from House number 5?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: What do we see coming up on the right?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: On the right, you can see the mosque and the damage done to the mosque. This is the area where we parked the vehicles. There were some members of the Red Cross there. These, I believe, are the imams.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: I notice, by the way, that there are a lot of leaves on the trees during this time period. We have seen evidence of photographs taken on April 16 where there were no leaves on the trees. Does this give you a sense of perhaps the time when this video was taken?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: This makes me think now that it was later in the tour, perhaps in May, early May.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: What are we seeing here?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: What you're seeing here is the surgical team with their equipment ready to extract the bodies from House number 5. You're also seeing the area where the vehicles were parked.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Who is that talking to the imam?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: That's an interpreter known as Dobrila.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: What happened to her?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: She was killed at the end of the tour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Do you know how she was killed?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: She was sniped in the head. She was shot in the head.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: By whom? Which side?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: What are we seeing now?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: You're looking now down towards the entrance of House number 5. You can note the number of the house. The imams were taken there first so that they could see the scene. This is Claire Podbielski, I believe, who was the most senior of the Red Cross people in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: What is happening now --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecutor please speak into the microphone?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: This is a picture of me leading out another soldier with a blanket containing remains.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Did you have an opinion as to the duty that your officers and men were required to do that day?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: This was the reason I was there, personally. I didn't consider it our particular job to do this. I didn't like the younger soldiers doing it, and I thought it might help if I was there personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: I see we have a dog there.

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: The dog was tied up because it had been eating at the remains.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: What is happening now?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: Remains are being placed in the armoured vehicles for transportation. This is the larger structure that I mentioned earlier, closer to the road. The man on the right with the glasses is the new commanding officer of the regiment taking over.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Does that also give you a hint of when this video may have been taken?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: This means that the video was taken in May.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: And that would be Colonel Stewart?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: This is Colonel Stewart, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Is that you?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: This is me carrying out some smaller remains. Animals had been in the building and had removed parts of bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Were your men affected by what they had seen in House number 5?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, they were, yes. They were very distressed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: If we can go slowly here, please?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, this shows the entrance to that room. You're looking at the stove there, a lot of red tiles about. Again --

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: If you could stop there, please? No, back up and go back into that room.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters cannot hear the Prosecutor, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: If you could please back up the videotape so that we can see inside the house? Right there. If we could stop there, please? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Could you tell us what that shows?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: This shows the shot through the main doorway looking at the stove.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: If we can then go just a little bit ahead to show the inside of the main room? Right there, if we could stop? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: This now shows a shot of the sides of that or one part of that room. In the bottom left-hand corner, you can see the stove covered with red tiles and you can clearly see a charred beam which was the area of a body. This picture is taken after the bodies had been extracted.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Does this video give a pretty good idea of the size of the room from the entrance door to that room?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, it does. This is only one half of the room, though.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: The entrance door as you come into the room comes in to the --

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: On the right, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: So a person walking into a room from the entrance door would have, essentially, that view?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Thank you. We can continue. I think this may be the end of the video or near the end. That would be you over there?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: That's me on the left-hand side of the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Do you recall what you were doing at that time?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: We were looking for more remains, really. As I mentioned earlier, animals had been in the properties and had removed pieces of the body.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Can you tell us what's happening here?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: That's exactly what's happening here. Animals have taken what appear to be remains away with them. We were unsure of the bones we were finding, whether they were human or from what was fed to dogs. So we basically bagged everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Here it looks like he's picking up something that may be a hand grenade. Would that be a weapon of some sort?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, it wouldn't be. It would be a bone, a fragment of bone, or something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: I take it that a Red Cross person would not handle things like that?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, not at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Now, we've seen images of the body bags being placed into an armoured ambulance. Do you have any idea where the bodies were taken from Ahmici, where they were taken?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: I have no idea of their exact location.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: That would be the armoured ambulance?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: At this time, I would ask the usher to show the witness two final exhibits in this order.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit 166. The video cassette was marked 165.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: The quality of these next two photographs are not the best because they were taken from the video that we have just seen, but can you tell us what that shows?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: This is a still taken from the video looking towards the stove in that main room from the doorway.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: So this would be a view of someone entering that main room --

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, it would.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: -- from the hallway or the entranceway of the house?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Could we then show the next exhibit, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit 167.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Exhibit 167, what does that show?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: This shows a portion of the room from the right as you enter that room, the stove being in the bottom left-hand corner covered with red tiles.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: The stove is difficult to see because it's covered with red tiles. Just to verify this photograph, which comes from the videotape that we have just seen, could you look at Exhibit 87, which I'm hoping is still in front of you in that pile. Is it possible for you to just help us get our bearings and compare the two photographs? Because you have already described that the photographer in Exhibit 87 was essentially in a very similar place to the video camera operator in Exhibit 167. It might be useful if you could show us some landmarks that will confirm that.

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: You can clearly see the burnt beam in the centre of the room. The body would have been here (indicating) before it was removed. You can see in this area the plaster removed underneath the window, and above the window, exposed beam. Out of the window and out the back, you can see a sort of loading-type ramp.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: If you could show us Exhibit 87 and correlate the video image to the photographic image for us. Maybe placing them on the ELMO side by side is fine.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters cannot hear the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: The beam I'm talking about is here and here (indicating) in both pictures. The area of plaster under the window removed is here and here (indicating). Out of the window, you can just make out in this picture some sort of concrete loading ramp structure, and above the window an area of plaster removed and beam, supporting beam.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: I notice the beam is placed differently in the video image than in the photographic image. Why?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: That would have been removed looking for more remains.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Would it be fair to say that the video image was taken after the remains were removed from the room?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Now, yesterday, Captain Stevens, you referred to a person who you know as Dragan who you met in one of your trips to Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: I did, yes. That's the first time I went there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: And you had a sort of sign language conversation with that individual?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: I did, yes. It's difficult to describe the way the conversation went, but, yes, that was correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: You have been in the courtroom here today, and you were in the courtroom --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let's consider this. Are you going to make an application for identification, Mr. Moskowitz?

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: I intend to do so, yes, Your Honour. I will lay the foundation, if you wish. This morning I spoke to Captain Stevens and asked him, did he see anyone in the courtroom yesterday who looked like the man he saw in 1993 whom he had the conversation with. Captain Stevens told me that, yes, he did see someone in the courtroom who was very similar to that person. I asked him, "Where did that person sit in the courtroom?"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, don't say any more. There's been no previous evidence of identification, merely that it was somebody called Dragan.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Someone he had -- I mean, he had a face-to-face conversation, admittedly, five years ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Five years ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: I think the quality of the identification will have to be considered by the Court, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, but it's a question of whether, effectively, a dock identification should be allowed. Mr. Radovic, I address you merely as counsel, but there may be others who have objections, but is there anything the Defence want to say about this before we rule on it?

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you for having given me the floor, Your Honour. We oppose this kind of identification. First of all, we are speaking about direct identification here in the courtroom, and previously, the witness was not even asked to give a description of the person he had talked to. In addition to that, the witness had an opportunity of seeing all the accused here yesterday, and he could have directed his glance at one person which, to him, may seem similar to that particular person. He is also talking about similarities. So pointing a finger at a person who is similar to the person that the witness had talked to, in principle, should not mean a thing. In addition to that, what would that mean? Identification of a person that the witness spoke to in sign language? Because the witness was speaking English, and the person who is being identified, allegedly the accused, was speaking Croatian or, rather, Bosnian. So I really do not see what circumstance this identification should relate to. At any rate, we are opposed to the identification because we do not know what count of the indictment we're talking about and in relation to what the witness should identify this person. The Prosecutor is not even saying this. The Prosecutor is saying, "We want to identify a person who is similar to the person whom the witness had talked to." I was a bit taken by surprise by your question, Your Honour. I wasn't following the Prosecutor very carefully. I didn't think it was all that important to us, although this surprise that the Prosecutor is proposing now on the second day of the questioning of the witness concerned, the witness has been watching the accused for two days now, and then today while he was preparing for the second day, he decided to opt for identification. If any identification is necessary, then it should have taken place straight away. That is what I wish to say in the roughest possible terms. Nothing further, Your Honour. My colleague, Ms. Glumac, is going to say something to support what I have said, with your permission, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Your Honour, this kind of sight identification in courtrooms is restrictively applied in our country and are practically prohibited by our law. In other places, whether applied, they are done in a very restrictive manner. So this would mean a violation of such rules. This kind of behaviour by the Prosecutor violates these rules. It is not only a question of the witness being here yesterday, but also he said earlier on in his statement, he did not mention a single person who would come -- not a single person was mentioned who would be subjected to identification here. Also, the fact remains that this process has been going on for quite some time now, that these proceedings have been going on for quite some time now, and the Captain probably had an opportunity of seeing these people in pictures on a number of occasions, because these are persons whose pictures are appearing in newspapers. So even if this identification were to be carried out, it has no value whatsoever. This kind of procedure, allowing this kind of thing, trying to recognise a person who would only be similar to someone who was seen such a long time ago, I think this should not be allowed. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: May I respond to that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes, please, Counsel Puliselic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I fully concur with what my colleagues, Mr. Radovic and Ms. Glumac, said. I believe that such a way of identification is unacceptable. At the least, from time to time, the places where the accused are sitting should be changed from time to time if one intends to do this in the future. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The danger of the dock identification, of course, is that the witness will look at the dock, see the man in the dock, and then identify him as the person he's seen before. This case is rather different. This witness did have an opportunity of observing the man he spoke to. There are six defendants, not one. This is not a national court. As is being observed often, national courts, of course, do not allow dock identifications. But in this case, the Chamber feels that it's in a position to weigh any identification which is made and decide what weight to give it. Of course, it's not a precedent for dock identifications generally, but merely deals with this particular instance. We propose to allow the Prosecutor to proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Captain Stevens, have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Perhaps, Mr. Moskowitz, you could briefly deal with the point that was made. Which count, counsel asks, is this relevant to?

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: This would be relevant, Your Honour, to Count 1, having to do with persecution, and it connects a defendant or an accused to that count through his statements to this witness regarding admissions of killings. That would go to the persecution count and a particular defendant. So I propose to ask this witness whether he has an opportunity to observe the people in this courtroom and whether he has an ability to identify, with some degree of certainty, an individual in this courtroom who matches the person whom he saw and spoke with in 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: I put it to you, Captain Stevens, have you had an opportunity, during the last few days, to look around the courtroom, and do you see anyone in this courtroom who you can say resembles the person you spoke to in 1993 and who identified himself as Dragan?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Can you tell us where that person is sitting?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: The person is sitting at the rear right, as I look at him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Would you describe whether or not he has facial hair?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: He didn't then. He does now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: How certain are you that this is the person you spoke with?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: I'm 99 per cent certain. When someone tells you they've killed 32 people, you don't forget their face in a hurry.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: At this point, that would end my direct examination. We would tender Exhibits 160 through 167.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: If I may make a comment, I think Counsel Radovic was right in saying that, in future, before asking a witness to identify one of the accused, you should ask the witness to describe the person. Please do so in future. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Mr. President, excuse me, I probably should make clear for the record that the person identified by the witness is, in fact, Dragan Papic so that the record is clear on that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Have you finished?

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. I was not clear on that. May I now turn to Counsel Pavkovic and ask whether he is in a position to tell us who is going to cross-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. I don't know whether the time would be right now to take a break, and then, perhaps, after the break, we could tell you the order of the attorneys who intend to question the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Because we would also like to agree amongst ourselves on the order in which questions should be put.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes. Of course, in principle and according to your own standards, Counsel Puliselic should start, but if he's not prepared to do so, we can wait until after the coffee break. It will be a 30-minute break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Counsel Pavkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I can inform you that the witness will, first of all, be cross-examined by Counsel Petar Pulisevic, then I will have some questions, and then Counsel Ranko Radovic, and Mrs. Jadranka Slokovic-Glumac after that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Puliselic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stevens, good morning to you.

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: You said that in Ahmici, in 1993, you met a man by the name of Dragan and that he told you that he alone or with somebody else had killed 32 Muslim men; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: I got the impression that he alone killed 32 men, and that he was proud of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Can you describe to us what that individual looked like on the occasion?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: That individual was wearing a camouflage jacket with darker civilian trousers and something like Wellington's on his feet. He had no head-dress but he was carrying an AK-47 rifle.

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: You said that that individual did not have a beard; is that not so?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: That's correct, he didn't have a beard at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us whether you noticed anything else particular on that individual?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: I can't tell anything other than that apart from he appeared tired. He was a strongly built man and he was fairly tall. That was it.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I didn't get the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Could you repeat your question, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Can the witness tell us how tall Dragan was more or less in centimetres, approximately how tall in centimetres?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: In centimetres, 180 to 190. One metre 80 to one metre 90.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, at that time, what kind of hair did he have? Did he have short hair, medium-length hair, longer hair? What was his hair like?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: Medium length to long, medium to long.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Did you perhaps remember the colour of his eyes when you recall events so exactly, events that took place five years ago?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't remember the colour of his eyes, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: You said that you talked to the individual by using sign language, as far as I recall; is that true? Yes?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Can you explain to us how you talked by using signs? What signs did he use to explain that he had killed 32 Muslims?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: He made a movement across his throat, he kept repeating the word "Muslim man," and because I couldn't get an idea of how many people he was referring to, he drew it in the ground, "32."

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: How were you able to conclude that he was talking about 32 Muslims? Could he not have said that in a neighbouring village, 32 Croats, for example, had been killed?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, he kept saying the word "Muslim man," "Muslim man," throughout the conversation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: All right. But how were you able to conclude that he -- he was the one who did it? Perhaps he was describing the killings done by somebody else. How can you know precisely on the basis of sign language that that was actually what happened?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know. All I know is that the impression he gave me was that he was indicating to me that he personally has killed 32 people, either that day or prior to that day, and he was pleased with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Very well. You said that that is your impression. But can you be absolutely precise and definite in saying that it was the case that he had killed 32 Muslims? Can you be absolutely definite on that point and that your conclusion is the right one on the basis of the signs that he used to converse with you?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: I travelled a lot through Central Bosnia and on occasions met soldiers who, when more relaxed, boasted and bragged about their achievements. I am quite comfortable with the fact that this man was telling me that he had killed 32 people himself. I have no doubt about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: You said yesterday, and that was recorded in the transcript, that you concluded that he or his friends had killed 32 Muslims. Now you claim that it was him.

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: I stick with what I said yesterday, either he or his friends.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: However, today you said that it was him and not his friends.

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: That's a mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: What is a mistake? What was said yesterday or what was said today?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: Today was a mistake. I felt that either he and his friends had done this.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: When was that exactly, the day and time that you met this Dragan?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: I have no recollection of the time, and as I mentioned earlier, the days were difficult to identify. I personally feel that it was the next day, the day after the village was attacked.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Therefore, the time of the day, can you tell us that?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: In the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: You can't tell the time exactly. You just say that it was in the afternoon; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: How come you can note these various details about the man, you remember that and that you had been shown signs, and from that you conclude that, according to your opinion, you conclude very precise conclusions, whereas you cannot state the time?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: At this particular period in our tour of duty, we were travelling everywhere to every conflict in every village to try and stop what was happening. It was extremely difficult to try and keep track of time and days.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: During your stay in the area, you met many people, and I find it a little strange that you remember so well faces and can describe a man after a time lapse of five and a half years.

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: As I mentioned earlier, you don't forget the face of someone who says they've killed so many people or suggest they've killed so many people. No one else that I had met during that tour had admitted to something as big as that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: During this contact of yours, was anybody else present, that is to say, your meeting?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: I believe there was someone with me, but I have no other recollection of that. I didn't walk off to find this man on my own. I wouldn't have done that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Did you happen to see this man, Dragan, previously?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, not at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Did you see him afterwards, after the event?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: I never saw him again after that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: So you only saw him once in your entire life?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: I saw him once on that day for approximately 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: How come yesterday, in this courtroom, when speaking about Dragan, you did not mention that you would be able to recognise him and how come you did not say yesterday that he was present in the courtroom?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: I didn't know at what stage and who to inform that I recognised this man, and I spent most of yesterday looking at the screen in front of me rather than the people in the court.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Let me go back to the question I asked a moment ago. How come you don't know who was with you at that time whereas you know many other details connected with the talk you had through sign language with Dragan?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: All the soldiers in my regiment are known to me. I'm comfortable with them. If I needed some protection or someone to move with me, I would pick someone nearby. I wouldn't have a particular person with me. I wouldn't really notice who the person was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Is it not strange to you that after so much time has gone by that you recognise an individual and describe these details and the details of your talk? It seems to me not quite acceptable, these kind of impressions on your part.

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: When I left the courtroom yesterday at the end of the day, I realised that I had seen the man that I saw that day, and I mentioned this to Mr. Moskowitz this morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: You said a moment ago that you didn't look around the courtroom yesterday because your attention was taken up with other things, the screen and so on. Now this is contrary to that.

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: I actually said that most of the time yesterday I was looking at the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Can you really be so sure that that Dragan is precisely this individual sitting here whom you pointed out, because it is a serious matter?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: I understand the seriousness of it, and I'm 99 per cent sure that that's the man I saw that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: That means that you do allow for the possibility that it is not him if you are 99 per cent sure.

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: The beard. As I mentioned before, he didn't have a beard. That's the small percentage. I didn't see him with a beard. He has a beard now.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have no further questions. I would just like to express my displeasure at this type of identification process because I think that this type of identification is unacceptable and that the Prosecutor should at least, before identification, tell the witness to describe an individual, what he looks like, and to give other details which are important for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Counsel Pavkovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Captain, I am Counsel Petar Pavkovic. You said yesterday that in May 1993 you came to Bosnia. Can you be more precise?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: In May 1993, I left Bosnia. I arrived in November 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, how many times were you in Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: Three times that I recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you set the time of your sojourn in Ahmici? When was that?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: The first time we were operating in another village and got there later in the day. That's why I know it was in the afternoon. We were running out of daylight, so we returned to the base and came back I think the following day.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: You said yesterday that during your first day in Ahmici, in Upper Ahmici, Gornji Ahmici, in a house, that you saw the burnt body of a child and of an older man; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: You then said that in the basement of that same house, you saw at least one male and several children and that they were all burnt.

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't believe I said a male. Another adult and several children, yeah. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I agree with what you say now. Tell me, please, was that recorded at the time? Was it filmed? Yes. Are the photographs which were shown by the Prosecution yesterday and which show the burnt bodies -- let us suppose that it was of a child and an adult -- are those the photographs in question?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: They are photographs from that building, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: The photographs that the Prosecution presented yesterday, are those the photographs?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: They are, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you explain how come that not everything was filmed then on location? We saw on the photographs only one body, the dead burnt body of a man, and something which would correspond to the burnt body of a child, and according to your description, we see that there are several individuals. How come the others were not filmed? Can you explain this to us, please?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: The others were filmed and, in fact, a picture of that I took myself shows the adult male in the doorway and a child on the doorstep. There are many pictures of this particular scene.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, you yesterday had previously discussed these events with somebody.

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: I previously discussed them? I don't understand that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Did you talk to the Prosecution's investigator about the events in Ahmici during your time of service there?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: I'm not sure who you mean by that, what person.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Not a person, but I am thinking of the investigators from the Prosecution's office. Did somebody from the side of the Prosecution and the Prosecution's investigators talk to you about these events? Did you tell anybody about these events?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I did, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: That was about four or five months ago in England.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Let us now go back to one detail of your first visit to Ahmici and what you have just said about the burnt bodies. Do you remember what you said then on the occasion?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: Exactly?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, exactly. Did you say what you told the Court yesterday and what you told me and all of us here today?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't really understand the question. I described a scene --

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honours, if I may, can I present the witness with this portion of his statement because this is important for us?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: You said, Captain, on the occasion, and this was on the 25th and 28th of November, 1996, you said the following --

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Could we have the page, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: I have the Croatian translation, and it is page 10 of the Croatian translation. Mr. President, may I present this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: "I went towards the house and looked at the basement and saw the bodies of an adult and two children. They were burnt. On the way to the door, there was a man and a boy from that house. They were also burnt." That is what you said about that event. Do you see the difference now? You are talking about an adult body and two children's bodies and then you say another adult man and a boy from the house, and here you have been speaking about several children, particularly in the basement of the house, and then you speak of another child and an adult.

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: There were bodies in two areas of the house, an adult male and a child on the -- in the doorway.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's exact.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Just for the information of the Court, Your Honour, page 8 and 9.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Eight and 9. Yes, yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was a male and a child on the doorsteps and in the doorway of that house, and in the basement or cellar of the same house, another adult and children, several children.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but what I have just shown you as having stated to the investigators is different from what you told the Court today in answer to my question today and when you were speaking freely yesterday. It is not a question of the fact that the bodies were located in different places in the same house but that there are a different number of individuals whom you saw; that is to say, the bodies you saw and the bodies that were burnt.

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: The way you phrase the questions about houses and burnt bodies, there were many houses with burnt bodies in them. At times I get confused what house you're referring to, what --

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: No. No, no, no. You could not have become confused because I said exactly what I have in mind. I just have in mind your first visit and this particular house, and you only spoke about that and you were precise in determining how many individuals and which individuals in your opinion. But never mind. You said that you became confused. I don't want to dwell, Mr. President, on that question any longer --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Mr. Moskowitz?

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm frankly confused as to what the distinction is between the statement in the written form and the testimony given by this witness, and perhaps if Defence counsel, Mr. Pavkovic, could be a little more precise on where he sees the distinction, it may make it easier for the witness to respond.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't know whether you have, perhaps, been misled by my questions, so if necessary I can repeat all of this, if you deem this necessary. If you wish, I can ask the witness once again, but I feel that there is no need for doing that. The differences are obvious, and there is no need to go back into all of that. Moreover, we showed just now where all of this is stated, actually, in the written statements that you have as well. So this can clearly be interrelated, and one can see whether the difference that I'm referring to does exist or does not exist and whether I'm justified in showing how substantially different these statements are, the ones he made yesterday and today, and the one he made previously that is recorded in writing. If you feel that it is unnecessary for me to go back to all of this, I may proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me put it right, just for the record. In the original of his written statement, the witness said, and I quote at the bottom of page 8: "I went over to the side of the house and looked into a cellar and saw the bodies of an adult and two children," two children. And then at page 9: "They were burnt. There was a man and a boy in the doorway of this house as well. They were burnt as well. Either me or somebody in the group told Colonel Stewart and I took the Colonel to have a look. From the position of the bodies of the children, it looked as if they had been burnt alive." So I see there's only one discrepancy here. In the statement, mention is made of two children in the cellar, whereas here, in court, the witness spoke of a basement where there was the body of an adult and children.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: And several children.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Several children, yes, not two, but several children, yes, just to put the record straight. Let us move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Captain, yesterday, in response to a question that was leading, to quite an extent, and the transcript is here, and I would like you to clarify what you said, the Prosecutor asked whether you saw some examples of ethnic cleansing. That is literally the question that the Prosecutor put to you yesterday. First of all, could you please explain what you mean by that? How did you understand that?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: I mean by that the burning of people out of their houses, the burning of their property.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Who? Who is burning people? How? In which way? It is not clear. Could you give me a more detailed answer as to what you mean by that, but not in such general terms. I mean, specifically, in terms of a specific area, a specific period, on the basis of what you saw, you're saying that that, for you, was an example of ethnic cleansing. So if you know about this, could you give me some examples from the area where you were, which, in your opinion, would be cases that justify this, what you call, ethnic cleansing.

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: I think I referred to Ahmici as being the worst case that I'd seen. The reason I say that is because almost every house in the village, every Muslim house, had been burnt down. At this time, from Easter through to early May, in the valleys that were near our main base, this was happening all the time. It happened on both sides, but more so by the Croatian army, and this was the worst case of it that I'd seen.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: So that is what you mean by ethnic cleansing. May I remind you, also, of your statement, the one I presented to you a few minutes ago when we were talking about the burned bodies, may I remind you what you said about ethnic cleansing on that occasion. You also said it yesterday in the trial, so could you please clarify that a bit for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: With your permission, Mr. President, this is page 8 of the translation, again, where the witness says the following: "I remember towards the end of my tour of duty, ethnic cleansing was carried out around the BRITBAT camp at Novi Bila. There were Bosnian Muslim occupied houses around the camp. The officers' mess for BRITBAT was just outside the parameter of the camp amongst these Bosnian Muslim houses. I remember that when this ethnic cleansing commenced, members of the HVO actually entered the officers' mess and officers' quarters. Captains David Sherlock and Richard Waltier of BRITBAT had to go into the officers' mess and rescue the regimental colours. I remember that they saw the HVO soldiers in the officers' accommodation. Things in our base were very tense, and all of the BRITBAT soldiers in the camp were stood to. The Bosnian soldiers appeared to regroup." So I have pointed out a part of this witness's statement which is supposed to explain his views on ethnic cleansing, his perception of ethnic cleansing. So that is why I went back to this question. I also wanted to show him what he said on that occasion. Could he kindly now comment upon what I just read out?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: Any comment that I would like to make is that ethnic cleansing, as far as I understand it, is the driving out of occupants from their property and then setting fire to it, so that they have nowhere to return to.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I wish to put another question to the witness, and that will be related to his claims concerning a person named Dragan. And, of course, I shall not be repeating what my colleague Puliselic asked.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, Captain, did you communicate with this person in sign language only, as you said?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. I did know a few words in Serbo-Croatian, just like "dobar dan," "puska," that type of thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Did he know the English language?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: I'm pretty sure that he knew a few English words, but that was about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: On the basis of what were you sure that he knew some English?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, he did say a few English words, like "hello," and that's about it. I can't remember other English words that he said. He couldn't put a sentence together, but he could say a few words.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you remember some other words that you heard from him on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I can't, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: So that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I wish to draw the witness's attention to his statement once again, and in it, he claimed that this Dragan spoke a bit of English.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: What do you say to that? On that occasion, you told the investigator that he did speak a bit of English, that he spoke a little English. So you agree with me that it was more or less saying "hello" and things like that?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: I agree with that. "A bit" means he could say "hello" and a few other English words. That's it. That's what I mean by "a bit."

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: And you do not remember them today?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: I didn't remember them then, and I don't remember them now.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: In response to the questions put by my colleague, Attorney Puliselic, you said that you never saw this person again after that day when he showed this to you in sign language, what he and/or his friends did. After that, until the present day, did you ever see a photograph of his?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Not in the newspapers, or did someone point him out to you?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: Nobody pointed him out to me, and I have never seen any photographs in newspapers.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: No further questions, Your Honour. Thank you, Captain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Counsel Radovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Captain, I shall start with a somewhat easier question. My first question would be the following: In your assessment, how good is your memory in terms of faces? Let us forget this Dragan for the time being. Do you remember in your everyday life persons you encounter, their faces? Could you please give me a "yes" or "no" answer?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, not everybody.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember when you were in Bosnia whether you attended an event on the 20th of December, '92 in Novi Bila? These were folk dances, so I wish to remind you of that.

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: Do I remember that I attended an event? Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Did you attend it? Yes. That's what I'm asking.

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't remember attending an event, no, but I probably did. I attended several events in the company of Colonel Stewart.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Were you ever present when a folk dance group performed, a group performing folk dances?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: I believe there might have been an occasion, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us where these events took place?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I couldn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: When these events took place, the ones that you believe did take place, do you remember what kind of folk dances were shown? Were there only Croatian dances or was it a mixture of Croatian and Muslim and Serb dances and folk songs?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: I could not tell you anything about folk dancing or anything like that. I wouldn't have been concerned with any of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: I know, but if you were present, then you watched it and listened to it, right, if nothing else?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: If I was present, I was more concerned with the safety of Colonel Stewart than anything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: If you were concerned with the safety of Colonel Stewart, you also had to watch the faces of the persons who were present. So could you please look at the accused and tell me whether you remembered any face that performed at these events or was present at these events? Let us see how good your memory of persons is.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, could you please ask the Captain to get up, to walk up to the dock, to look at each and every one of the individuals who are accused, and to say whether he recognises any one of them as having been present at these folk dance performances? One moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Counsel Radovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Actually, there are two persons who are accused and who performed on that occasion, and I think that we will be able to prove this by showing a videotape later. This would be a good opportunity to see how good the Captain's memory is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Captain, can you see all of the defendants from the place where you're sitting? There are six defendants.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There's one just around the pillar there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Could you please stand and move a little bit so that you can see all of them? Can you answer the question put by the Defence counsel? You may sit.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Can you recognise anyone here as a person who performed on that occasion or not?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I can't.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: We have completed that part, and now we shall be moving on to Zenica. During your stay in Bosnia, you were a noncommissioned officer, to the best of my understanding; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Did your knowledge include ballistics, as you were a noncommissioned officer?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: It depends what you refer to as "ballistics." I know firearms pretty well.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: I'm referring to the properties of artillery and the possibilities offered by artillery. So I'm talking about cannons, guns, not infantry arms, not small arms, but artillery pieces?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: I'm not an expert in that field, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Some time ago, you said here that you were sure that Serbs were not in a position to be shelling Zenica with their artillery. Do you know, at that time, when Zenica was being attacked, how many kilometres away were the Serbian artillery positions?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: I know where they were sited on the ground, but I think it was probably something in the region of --

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: How many kilometres away from Zenica?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: Twenty-six to twenty-eight, something like that. It depended at what point on the feature they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Were there 130-millimetre guns within the Serbian artillery?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: There might well have been. I didn't see any.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Could a 130-millimetre-calibre gun, from a Serb position, actually fire at Zenica and reach Zenica?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: Possibly, depending on the charges. I'm not an artillery man.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Oh, I see. I'm asking you this because you were saying that it was not possible to hit Zenica from the Serbian positions. And I know that it is possible, not only because of what you said, the charges, I mean, but also because of the difference in altitude. Do you agree with what I said? Because Zenica is at a lower altitude than the place where the artillery pieces were. Am I saying all of this correctly?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: I presume so.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: So we have agreed, as far as military matters are concerned.

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: We've agreed on what?

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: On how far a gun can hit, how far a cannon, a gun, can hit. On how far, a cannon, a gun, can hit.

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: I said I'm a non-artillery officer. I'm an infantry man.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: I know that you're an infantry man. But since you made a statement in the domain of artillery, I had to ask you these things related to artillery. But I did say, before I started questioning you, that you were an infantry man.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: That would be all, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Counsel Slokovic-Glumac?

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Good day, Captain Stevens. I'm going to ask you about the house that you entered with this group of people. This was House number 5 you said, and that two bodies were found in it, one of an adult and one of a child, and that you assumed it was a child. Tell me, the body of the adult was near the window; right? We can, perhaps --

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: I'll probably need the pictures to point it out.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Yes. I need it too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Is it Prosecution Exhibit 164?

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Please show us where the body of the adult was, that is, of the person who you say was an adult.

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: In this area here (indicating).

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: The place that has been marked. So that is to the right of the door?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: The remains of that body, I mean, we saw on the picture that these were parts of a skeleton. That is the part we saw here.

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Please tell us, this other part where the body of the child was, what was there? We didn't see this on the recording. Were there bones there? Of course, these are very unpleasant questions, but we would like to know, what is it that you found there?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: There was a skull there of a small size. That's all that was there.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Thank you. These two rooms that were behind, you didn't go there because there was nothing there; right? Did you search them at all?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: We searched quickly through with sticks, through the rubble, but we didn't spend any time in there.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Can you, perhaps, tell us how big this room is? Actually, you've spoken in terms of feet, but I'm not very good at that. Could you please tell us in terms of metres how big the room was?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: I think it was about -- I'm not sure. I'm not very good with metres. Nine metres by four metres, five metres, something like that. Nine by five. It was about eighteen feet and ten feet wide, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. The stove that was against the wall, it was actually in the middle of this wall, in the central part, was it, the stove that we saw on the photograph?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: As you saw it on the photograph is as it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: We cannot tell because the perspective is not very accurate, so I'm asking you because you were actually there. It was somewhere towards the central part, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, it was, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: The door here, the entrance to the room that leads to the upper room, that is the room on the left-hand side, how far away was this door from the stove; can you tell that?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: The door from the stove?

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Yes, the door from the stove.

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: Perhaps 7 or 8 feet, two metres something.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Did you perhaps notice a pipe going towards the chimney from this stove because this is usually a stove fired by wood? So was there a pipe there? I mean, we can't see it in the photograph, but do you perhaps remember seeing this kind of a pipe?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't remember seeing a pipe, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: On this side, you said that the only thing that was left were metal objects, like the stove. Did you see any other things made of metal in the house? Did you perhaps see springs from a bed mattress or something?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES STEVENS (Resumed)
utterances.text: I may well have done, but I don't recollect them.
